name: Sushilkumar Parekh
forbes_bio: Sushilkumar Pareks draws his wealth from a minority stake in Pidilite Industries, which is India's leading maker of adhesives and sealants.
The company was founded by his late brother, Balvant Parekh, in 1959.
His nephew Madhukar Parekh chairs the company and his younger brother Narendrakumar Parekh is the vice chairman.
Pidilite's range of products includes construction chemicals, art materials and organic pigments.
forbes_facts: Pidilite is best known for its iconic white glue, Fevicol, popularized over the decades with clever advertising.

name: Fumio Kaneko
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Fumio Kaneko is the president of waste management company Daiei Kankyo, which he founded with three others in 1979.
The company has expanded into waste recycling, power generation using waste and soil remediation.
Daiei Kankyo was listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2022.
The company reported $560 million in revenue in the fiscal year through March 2025.

name: Lai Shixian
forbes_bio: Lai Shixian is an executive director and chief financial officer at Anta Sports, China's largest sportswear company.
Lai is the brother-in-law of fellow Anta billionaires and executive directors Ding Shizhong and Ding Shijia.
Lai holds an EMBA from the China Europe International Business School.

name: Jeffrey Straubel
forbes_bio: JB Straubel is the founder and CEO of Redwood Materials and the former chief technology officer of Tesla.
A Stanford-educated engineer, Straubel was working on battery-powered planes in 2003 when he met Elon Musk at a campus lecture.
He joined Tesla as employee No. 5 in 2004, and drove the development of its battery packs and electric motors as CTO. He left the C-suite in 2019 but remains on the board.
He now runs Redwood Materials, a Nevada-based electric vehicle battery recycling startup  he founded in 2017.

He now runs Redwood Materials, a Nevada-based electric vehicle battery recycling startup he founded in 2017. It has since expanded to making battery materials from recovered metals. In 2025, Redwood also began building and selling battery storage systems for data centers..

name: Wang Han
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023-2026); Forbes annual (2016-2023); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Han's wealth mainly comes from shares in Juneyao Air that he inherited from his deceased father Wang Junyao, a co-founder of Juneyao Group.
Juneyao also has business interests in retailing, education and food.
Wang's other investment stakes include Shanghai AJ Group, Hubei Juneyao Great Health Diary and Wuxi Commercial Mansion.

name: Johanna Braun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Johanna Braun owns 10% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
Her father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
A sixth-generation family member, Johanna is the youngest daughter of Ludwig Georg. Her sister, Anna Maria, is CEO of B. Braun.
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments
forbes_facts: Johanna Braun is a member of the board of the B. Braun Foundation, which works in education, science and public health in the field of human medicine.
B. Braun has been operating in Africa for more than 60 years, and now has subsidiaries in Zambia, Algeria, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.

name: Jorge Gallardo Ballart
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2022); Hurun Global (2020-2022)
forbes_bio: Jorge Gallardo Ballart's father founded pharmaceutical company Almirall in 1943 in Barcelona.
After their father died in 1988, Jorge and his brother Antonio took over running Almirall; the company is publicly traded.
Jorge is executive president of Almirall, which had about $900 million revenues in 2020.
In 2018, Almirall announced the acquisition of five products from the dermatology division of Allergan.
Ballart's son, Carlos Gallardo Piqué, was appointed chairman of Almirall in 2022.

name: Sidney Kimmel
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Sidney Kimmel founded apparel company Jones Group more than four decades ago; it owned brands including Stuart Weitzman and Nine West.
In 2014, he sold the company for $2.2 billion to private equity firm Sycamore Partners.

His production company Sidney Kimmel Entertainment was responsible for movies including ?The Place Beyond The Pines? and ?Crazy Rich Asians,? before he sold a majority stake in 2022 to London-based investment firm Centricus.
Kimmel has donated more than $200 million to Thomas Jefferson University over the past two decades, much of which has gone to cancer research.

name: Vladimir Voronin
forbes_bio: Vladimir Voronin is the founder of FSK Group, one of the largest housing developers in Russia.
Since 2022 Voronin has bought Russian assets of foreign companies at a discount, including Belgian mineral company Sibelco, Swedish residential developer Bonava and U.S. glass maker Guardian Glass.
In the 2000s, his father Alexander Voronin was a major shareholder of one of the largest construction groups in Moscow with revenue of about $1 billion.
In 2005 Alexander lost the construction assets in a corporate war with billionaire Suleiman Kerimov, who later sold the assets to Russian billionaire Oleg Deripaska.

name: Surin Upatkoon
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Low-profile tycoon Surin Upatkoon made his fortune across sectors from insurance to telecom.
Most of his wealth comes from selling a 10% stake in Thai telecom company InTouch in 2013.
He owns stakes in listed gaming company Magnum, financial services outfit MPHB Capital and textile firm MWE.
He started his career as a manager at MWE Weaving Mills in 1971 and rose through the ranks.
His son, Krian, is on the boards of MWE and Magnum, while Ivevei, the older of his two daughters, is on the board of MPHB Capital.
forbes_facts: Upatkoon is a Thai national but moved to Penang for school, stayed for work and has been a  Malaysia resident ever since.
In January 2025 he launched a selective capital reduction exercise to privatise  his financial services company MPHB Capital.

name: Melissa Ma
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2015)
forbes_bio: Melissa Ma is the wife of Robin Li, the CEO and chairman of Chinese search giant Baidu.
Melissa left Baidu in 2007 but returned as special assistant to the chairman a decade later, overseeing areas such as investments.
The Robin Li and Melissa Ma Science Library opened at Stanford University in 2017.

name: Michael Wisser
forbes_bio: Michael Wisser controls Wisag, a family-owned German facilities and logistics business.
The company, which was founded by his father, Claus, provides services that include aircraft loading and unloading, freight services and passenger transfers, and commercial cleaning.
Wisag has annual revenue of reported more than 3 billion euros, according to its most recent financial filings.
The company's motto is ?Let's end the impossible.?

name: Subbamma Jasti
forbes_bio: Subbamma Jasti inherited the assets of her husband Subba Rao Jasti, who died in 2023.
The biggest chunk of her inheritance is derived from the sale of a substantial stake in listed Suven Pharmaceuticals in 2022 to global private equity firm Advent International.
Jasti's son Venkateswarlu Jasti cofounded Suven Pharmaceuticals in 1989.
The Hyderabad company was demerged in 2020 when Suven Life Sciences, which focuses on neuroscience therapies, was spun off and listed separately.
forbes_facts: Her son Venkateswarlu Jasti ran a chain six of community pharmacies in the states of New York and New Jersey in the U.S. in the 1970s and 1980s.

name: Hisako Yamamoto
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Hisako Yamamoto is the daughter of Seven & I Holding's late honorary chairman Masatoshi Ito and gets her  wealth from her stake in the global retailing giant.
Her two siblings, Junro Ito and Yasuhisa Ito, are also billionaires based on their stakes.
Masatoshi Ito, who helped build 7-Eleven into a global giant, died in March 2023 at age 98.
Seven & i Holdings has 87,000 stores in 19 countries and nearly $80 billion in annual revenue.
In 2024, Canadian retail giant, Alimentation Couche-Tard made a $47 billion takeover bid for the company but withdrew in July 2025 citing the retailer's lack of cooperation during negotiations.
forbes_facts: The company also runs Denny's restaurants in Japan and owns department stores, supermarkets, and financial services firms.
The family was considering a $58 billion management buyout of the company but backed out in February 2025 citing financial issues.
In March 2025, Seven & I agreed to sell its York Holdings unit, which includes major supermarket chains and specialty retailers, to Bain Capital for $5.4 billion.
